Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. I ran this by Evelyn (privacy lead) and Dev (solutions infra) and we pulled together a short package attached: redwood_tia_summary.pdf and sccs_mapping_v1.xlsx. Highlights in the PDF include: 

- Data flows: we enumerate personal data types (telemetry, PII in prompts/outputs, token metadata) and where persisted (hosted vs. customer-dedicated).
- Legal guardrails: for hosted we rely on DPA + SCCs (EU standard clauses) where required; dedicated/private customers get contractual clauses plus customer-managed KMS option.
- Risk mitigations: automatic KV prefix caching avoidance for regulated datasets, configurable data retention windows, and optional at-rest envelope encryption with customer keys.

Quick notes for your DPIA: our hosted environment routes model inference through EU regions by default for EU customers; fallthrough to non-EU is controlled by routing policy and audit logs show region selection per-request. The mapping sheet lists which components handle data and the corresponding contract/control.

If you want, Evelyn can join a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the package and answer mapping questions — she can also pull SOC 2 control references if you need explicit control IDs.

Lisa — thanks for the clear asks. Quick status and deliverables below (Evelyn/Dev in copy to own the artifacts):

- SCC mapping: we updated sccs_mapping_v2.xlsx (attached) to include a column "application mode" (DPA, Dedicated, Private) and an explicit note per row. Procurement can cite the DPA clauses for hosted and the private deployment contract for on-prem/Dedicated.
- BYOK/HSM: BYOK is available for Dedicated customers today. Dev attached a short admin playbook excerpt and the supported HSM providers (AWS KMS HSM via CloudHSM; Azure Key Vault HSM; on-prem HSM integrations). We also include the admin flow URL: https://drive.example.com/file/d/1a2b3cTIAsummary (internal admin guide - shareable link).
- Auditor-facing summary: included below, feel free to paste into your DPIA packet.

---- auditor-facing summary (copyable) ----
Redwood Inference maintains contractual and technical safeguards to minimize cross-border transfer risk. For hosted customers, data residency is selectable by region and is enforced by routing policies; transfers to non-EU regions occur only under documented fallback policies and are logged for auditability. Where transfers are necessary, Redwood executes the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) in the Data Processing Agreement and supplements legal safeguards with technical measures: in-transit TLS encryption for all requests, at-rest encryption, and optional customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated customers. Operational mitigations include short default retention windows for request metadata, KV-prefix caching controls to avoid retention of sensitive prefixes, continuous monitoring and alerting for cross-region routing, and periodic SOC 2 audits mapping controls to transfer risk. Residual risk is assessed as low-to-moderate for standard inference workloads; customers processing sensitive special category data should evaluate Private or Dedicated deployments with BYOK and reduced data retention settings.
---- end summary ----

Next steps: Evelyn will send the updated sccs_mapping_v2.xlsx and the SOC 2 control crosswalk in a follow-up email within the hour. If you confirm a 30-minute slot, we’ll have Evelyn run through the mapping and Dev will cover BYOK flows. Suggested time: 2026-12-02 15:00 CET / 09:00 ET.

Thanks — Jordan
